key_insight: Neural networks discover nonlinear water-wave candidates with near-machine-precision equation residuals, followed by rigorous residual certification and Lean-checked deductions.
engineering_relevance: The pipeline shows how machine-learning-based PDE discovery can be paired with auditable numerical error bounds and formal verification.
method: Train physics-informed neural networks without training data to learn wave profiles, speeds and, in continuation experiments, surface tension.
Freeze one candidate into a finite representation and bound its residual using interval arithmetic, including roundoff, truncation, aliasing and grid-to-continuum errors.
Use Lean to machine-check deductions from certified numerical bounds to the residual theorem.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports recovery of Stokes waves, Crapper waves and Wilton ripples, discovery of new high-amplitude candidates, and rigorous uniform residual certification for one candidate.
watch_item: A certified small residual does not by itself establish existence or uniqueness of a nearby exact solution, and certification is reported for only one candidate.
paper_title: Rigorously Certified Neural-Network Computation of Nonlinear Water Waves at Near-Machine Precision
